en.html:
A small handcart piled with metal. To call it noise pollution is to speak very kindly. Every step, rattle-clatter, and then the corridor repeats the whole argument for anybody whose ears survived the first hearing.

But during a race, the paddock recognizes neither night nor rest. Mechanics hammer through till morning, getting everything they can from their machines. Riders sleep to that hammering. Their lullaby, apparently.

In this conductorless xylophone concert, our cart is only one more instrument. Fortunately, we can inconvenience nobody. Everybody is already sufficiently inconvenienced.

金物を積んだ小型の<ruby>手引車<rt>リヤカー</rt></ruby>は、控えめに批評しても
騒音公害に違いない。
　進むたび、がらがらがちゃがちゃと音が鳴り、それ
が廊下に反響するとなれば耳障りもここに極まる。

　だがレース中のパドックには夜もなければ安息の時
もない。
　メカニックは徹夜で鎚を振るって騎体調整に最善を
尽くし、騎手は彼の鎚音を子守唄にして眠る。

　この指揮者不在の鉄琴演奏会とでも云うべき状況下
で、手引車の立てる騒音ごときは、所詮響きの一つに
過ぎなかった。
　誰にも迷惑を掛けずに済むのは幸いなことだ。

No reason at all.

This contempt for the police team is entirely reasonable. I cannot find even one word to oppose it. Thanks to being so thoroughly beneath consideration, one half of my calculation has succeeded.

The other half—the important half, not even comparable—has produced nothing.

...Though that nothing is also a result. A result nobody wanted, but it has come anyway.

en.html:
If I enter tomorrow's final, it will be to stay beside the host probably hiding among the racing tsurugi and stop it at the instant of hatching. Without Muramasa armored around me, the whole exercise has no meaning.

But look from any direction: Muramasa is unmistakably a true-forged tsurugi. Enter her as she is and we might as well announce that the police are keeping their own warrior.

Therefore, refitting.

Fortunately, Muramasa's colors and shape are not altogether unlike Hot Bolt's. Make enough alterations and she could perhaps pass for a modified Hot Bolt.

If that can be done, what better method is there?
